Getting started with IonFamilies

2026-11-11

Source: vignettes/IonFamilies.qmd

Introduction

One compound in an LC-MS experiment gives many features: its protonated or deprotonated molecule, other adducts such as [M+Na]+, in-source fragments such as [M+H-H2O]+, and the isotopes of all of these. Together they form the compound’s ion family. Recognising ion families reduces redundancy and helps to work out the neutral mass of unknown compounds.

groupFeatures() from the MsFeatures and xcms packages groups features that probably come from the same compound (similar retention time, correlated abundances across samples, similar peak shapes). It deliberately stops there. IonFamilies takes the groups and annotates, within each group,

  1. isotope patterns, with MetaboCoreUtils::isotopologues(), which checks mass differences and intensity ratios, and
  2. adducts and fragments, by neutral-mass voting with a rule list: a neutral mass is suggested when two or more features of a group can be explained as different ions of it.

All supported neutral-mass hypotheses are kept and ranked. The annotations are meant as hints for what to check, so the default rule list is long and recall is preferred over precision. Results are written to the featureDefinitions() of the XcmsExperiment: the isotopes and adduct columns use CAMERA’s text syntax, and the grouping itself is the feature_group column written by groupFeatures(). The vignette How neutral-mass voting works explains the method step by step.

Related packages

  • CAMERA does grouping, isotope and adduct annotation, but works on the legacy xcmsSet class. IonFamilies re-implements its neutral-mass voting for groupFeatures() groups and keeps all hypotheses, ranked, instead of one per feature.
  • InterpretMSSpectrum (findMAIN()) ranks main-adduct hypotheses for a single spectrum. RAMClustR uses it after its own clustering.
  • cliqueMS annotates one sample at a time with its own grouping.
  • MetaboAnnotation matches features against compound databases. It complements the database-free annotation here.

Installation 

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stanstrup/IonFamilies")

Grouping features

We use the small example data set that comes with xcms: an XcmsExperiment with peak detection, alignment and correspondence already done. First the features are grouped by retention time, then the groups are split by the correlation of the features’ abundances across samples.

library(xcms)
#> Warning: replacing previous import 'S4Arrays::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' by
#> 'DelayedArray::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' when loading 'SummarizedExperiment'
library(MsFeatures)
library(IonFamilies)
library(dplyr)

x <- loadXcmsData("xmse")
x <- groupFeatures(x, SimilarRtimeParam(diffRt = 10))
x <- groupFeatures(x, AbundanceSimilarityParam(threshold = 0.7,
                                               transform = log2))
table(lengths(split(featureGroups(x), featureGroups(x))))
#> 
#>   1   2   3   4   6 
#> 184  55  13   3   1

With raw data available, EicSimilarityParam() would add a third step that compares peak shapes.

Isotopes

annotateIsotopes() searches isotope patterns within each group. The representative intensity of a feature is its median over the samples given by subset (all samples by default).

x <- annotateIsotopes(x, IsotopologueParam(ppm = 10, tolerance = 0.005))
fd <- as.data.frame(featureDefinitions(x))
fd %>%
    filter(isotopes != "") %>%
    select(mzmed, rtmed, feature_group, isotopes) %>%
    head()
#>       mzmed    rtmed feature_group   isotopes
#> FT033 300.2 3404.692    FG.002.001    [1][M]+
#> FT034 301.0 2789.217    FG.006.001    [4][M]+
#> FT035 301.2 3404.692    FG.002.001  [1][M+1]+
#> FT037 302.0 2790.972    FG.006.001  [4][M+1]+
#> FT069 329.2 3642.045    FG.089.001   [36][M]+
#> FT070 330.2 3643.682    FG.089.001 [36][M+1]+

isIsotopologue() identifies the heavy isotopologues, for example to remove them before statistics:

count(fd, heavy_isotopologue = isIsotopologue(isotopes))
#>   heavy_isotopologue   n
#> 1              FALSE 307
#> 2               TRUE  44

Adducts and fragments

annotateAdducts() uses the rules in defaultAdductRules(), which come from the commonMZ package and are expanded to one to four molecules per ion.

rules <- defaultAdductRules("positive")
nrow(rules)
#> [1] 159
head(rules)
#>        name nmol charge massdiff oidscore quasi  ips
#> 1    [M+H]+    1      1 1.007276        1     1 1.00
#> 2   [2M+H]+    2      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 3   [3M+H]+    3      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 4   [4M+H]+    4      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 5  [M+2H]2+    1      2 2.014552        2     0 0.75
#> 6 [2M+2H]2+    2      2 2.014552        2     0 0.75

Every feature of a group is tried as every quasi-molecular ion in the rules (such as [M+H]+ or [M+Na]+). A neutral mass M becomes a hypothesis when at least one other feature of the same group is explained by some rule as an ion of that M. Heavy isotopologues found in the previous step are left out.

x <- annotateAdducts(x, AdductVoteParam(polarity = "positive"))
hints <- adductHints(x)

adductHints() returns all hypotheses as one table, with one row per hypothesis and feature. hypothesis ranks the hypotheses within a group by score (the summed rule scores), and n_ions is the number of features that support M.

To see how this works, we look at the group with the most competing hypotheses:

group <- hints %>%
    slice_max(hypothesis, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    pull(feature_group)

fd <- featureDefinitions(x) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    mutate(feature = row_number())

fd %>%
    filter(feature_group == group) %>%
    select(mzmed, rtmed, isotopes)
#>       mzmed    rtmed   isotopes
#> FT040 305.1 3504.720           
#> FT093 351.1 3503.953   [15][M]+
#> FT095 353.1 3504.855 [15][M+2]+

The group has 3 features. One of them is a heavy isotopologue ([M+1]+ or [M+2]+) and gets no adduct hypotheses. The hypotheses of the others are:

group_hints <- hints %>%
    filter(feature_group == group) %>%
    left_join(select(fd, feature, mzmed), by = "feature") %>%
    arrange(hypothesis, mzmed)

group_hints %>%
    select(hypothesis, M, n_ions, score, mzmed, adduct, rank)
#>   hypothesis        M n_ions score mzmed           adduct rank
#> 1          1 350.0927      2  1.75 305.1     [M+H-HCOOH]+    1
#> 2          1 350.0927      2  1.75 351.1           [M+H]+    1
#> 3          2 282.1108      2  1.50 305.1          [M+Na]+    2
#> 4          2 282.1108      2  1.50 351.1    [M+H+CHOONa]+    2
#> 5          3 368.1033      2  1.25 305.1 [M+H-H2O-HCOOH]+    3
#> 6          3 368.1033      2  1.25 351.1       [M+H-H2O]+    3

Each hypothesis explains the same features in a different way. The best one, M = 350.093, reads them as [M+H-HCOOH]+ and [M+H]+. The others are alternatives that the long rule list also allows. This is why the annotations are hints: they tell you what to check, not what the compound is. Note that this example data set is small and of low mass accuracy, so the hypotheses here are weak. The section Working with plain vectors shows a clear case.

The adduct column

rank is the rank of a hypothesis for one feature (1 = most plausible). The adduct column of featureDefinitions() shows the nBest best hypotheses of each feature as text in CAMERA’s format, best first. The default is nBest = 3. formatAdducts() rewrites the column with another nBest without recomputing anything:

x1 <- formatAdducts(x, nBest = 1)

fd %>%
    mutate(nBest_1 = featureDefinitions(x1)$adduct) %>%
    filter(feature_group == group) %>%
    select(mzmed, nBest_3 = adduct, nBest_1)
#>       mzmed                                                       nBest_3
#> FT040 305.1 [M+H-HCOOH]+ 350.093 [M+Na]+ 282.111 [M+H-H2O-HCOOH]+ 368.103
#> FT093 351.1       [M+H]+ 350.093 [M+H+CHOONa]+ 282.111 [M+H-H2O]+ 368.103
#> FT095 353.1                                                              
#>                    nBest_1
#> FT040 [M+H-HCOOH]+ 350.093
#> FT093       [M+H]+ 350.093
#> FT095

One hypothesis per feature

bestHypotheses() reduces the hints to at most one neutral mass per feature, as CAMERA’s final result did. Hypotheses are accepted from the best down, and one is skipped if any of its features is already explained:

bestHypotheses(hints) %>%
    filter(feature_group == group)
#>   feature feature_group hypothesis rank        M       adduct n_ions score
#> 1      40    FG.030.001          1    1 350.0927 [M+H-HCOOH]+      2  1.75
#> 2      93    FG.030.001          1    1 350.0927       [M+H]+      2  1.75
#>   intensity
#> 1  822876.7
#> 2  822876.7

Stored parameters

The parameters used are stored in the object:

S4Vectors::metadata(x)$IonFamilies
#> $isotopes
#> Object of class "IsotopologueParam"
#>  ppm: 10 
#>  tolerance: 0.005 
#>  polarity: positive 
#>  value: into 
#>  subset: all samples 
#> 
#> $adducts
#> Object of class "AdductVoteParam"
#>  rules: 159 rules, 5 quasi-molecular
#>  ppm: 10 
#>  mzabs: 0.005 
#>  polarity: positive 
#>  value: into 
#>  subset: all samples 
#>  nBest: 3

Working with plain vectors

All functions also work without xcms. Here are the ions of 2-furoylglycine (M = 169.0375), a marker of coffee intake, from one feature group:

mz <- c(95.0124, 124.0392, 152.0342, 170.0445, 171.0496, 192.0275,
        377.0300, 393.0019)
int <- c(71.6, 81.4, 49.8, 100, 4.33, 11.3, 1.76, 1.82)
grp <- rep("FG.1", length(mz))

iso <- annotateIsotopes(mz, IsotopologueParam(), intensity = int,
                        groups = grp)
hints <- annotateAdducts(mz, AdductVoteParam(), intensity = int,
                         groups = grp, exclude = isIsotopologue(iso))
data.frame(mz, isotopes = iso,
           adduct = formatAdducts(hints, nBest = 2, nFeatures = length(mz)))
#>         mz  isotopes
#> 1  95.0124          
#> 2 124.0392          
#> 3 152.0342          
#> 4 170.0445   [1][M]+
#> 5 171.0496 [1][M+1]+
#> 6 192.0275          
#> 7 377.0300          
#> 8 393.0019          
#>                                                                     adduct
#> 1 [M+H - O=C=NCH3 (methyl isocyanate)]+ 151.027 [M+H-NH3-H2O-H2O]+ 147.055
#> 2                                   [M+H-HCOOH]+ 169.037 [M+H-CO]+ 151.027
#> 3                                        [M+H-H2O]+ 169.037 [M+H]+ 151.027
#> 4                                           [M+H]+ 169.037 [M+Na]+ 147.055
#> 5                                                                         
#> 6                                       [M+Na]+ 169.037 [M+2Na-H]+ 147.055
#> 7                                           [2M+K]+ 169.037 [4M+H]+ 94.005
#> 8                                                           [M+K]+ 354.041

Here the best hypothesis is the right one. Five ions agree on M = 169.037: the protonated molecule, the sodium adduct, the potassium adduct of the dimer, and two in-source fragments (losses of water and of formic acid). The feature at m/z 171.050 is the [M+1]+ isotope of the protonated molecule and is therefore left out:

hints %>%
    filter(hypothesis == 1) %>%
    mutate(mz = mz[feature], M = round(M, 4)) %>%
    select(mz, adduct, M)
#>         mz       adduct        M
#> 1 124.0392 [M+H-HCOOH]+ 169.0372
#> 2 152.0342   [M+H-H2O]+ 169.0372
#> 3 170.0445       [M+H]+ 169.0372
#> 4 192.0275      [M+Na]+ 169.0372
#> 5 377.0300      [2M+K]+ 169.0372
